description: Elevance Health is a health benefits provider, offering health care coverage and specialty insurance, such as dental, vision, and life. Elevance Health was formerly known as Anthem, and does business under its Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, Wellpoint, and Carelon brands.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
Elevance, formerly Anthem, calls itself the largest commercial insurer in the U.S., and contains the core brands of Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, Carelon, and Wellpoint.

The company developed its employee assistance program into the concierge service Associate CARE Service, which provides customized care for employees and their households, including support for mental illness, family distress, grief counseling, and substance abuse, all as part of associates’ benefits and at no extra cost.

 

In 2022, the Elevance Health Foundation invested more than $84 million in grants and sponsorships, and associates volunteered 135,199 hours and generated an additional $12.5 million in community support. The foundation made a three-year commitment to invest $90 million in partnerships and programs addressing racial inequity in maternal-child health, substance abuse disorders, and food as medicine.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
Elevance Health, which says it’s the largest commercial insurer in the U.S. as of 2022, is known for having a culture that recognizes that it’s people who make the company great.

  • Elevance Health underwent a corporate rebrand in June 2022, after being previously known as Anthem.

  • In 2022 the company laid off 642 employees, roughly 0.8% of its workforce.

  • Recognizing that different employees have different needs and preferences, Elevance Health devised a hybrid strategy that features four distinct “flex workstyles” that managers and direct reports can use based on their individual team needs.

  • In partnership with the She-Suite Brand Leadership Institute, Elevance Health launched a new program to advance high-potential women more quickly within the company.

  • Elevance encourages employees to celebrate each other through the IMPACT recognition program. Colleagues can give out the Go Above award and the Go Beyond award for stellar performance.

rankings.title: Fortune Modern Board 25
rankings.itemDescription: The health insurance provider’s board, including experts in the medical field and a who’s who of finance executives, also scores strongly in gender, racial, and age diversity. Its chair, Elizabeth Tallett, is a health care consultant and previously the CEO of pharmaceutical firm Transcell Technologies. Other board members include Elevance CEO Gail Boudreaux and Robert L. Dixon, former CIO of PepsiCo. Elevance’s stock is down 8% year to date, but the company plans to expand several care management programs and product offerings. Elevance hit a first-quarter profit of $2 billion, adding 1.3 million new members.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription:
Elevance Health continued its brisk recent pace of growth in 2022, boosted by acquisitions and by pandemic-related spending. Revenues rose 13% to $156.6 billion.

  • Elevance ended 2022 with 47.5 million members on its various health insurance plans. In the first quarter of 2023 it added another 1.3 million.

  • The health insurance giant agreed to purchase Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Louisiana for a reported $2.5 billion in December 2022, adding roughly 1.9 million patients to its books.

  • In June 2022 Elevance consolidated all of its health care services divisions, including prescriptions fulfillment, behavioral health, and at-home care, under the new Carelon brand.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: When the pandemic hit, insurance giant Anthem held listening sessions and developed fresh ways to support associates. The Associate CARE Community of Service was an online community—complete with 24/7 concierge service—that assisted employees in need of food, transportation, childcare, and more. (It has since been discontinued and replaced with other wellness benefits.) Anthem also realizes the value of self-care; during Mental Health Awareness Month in 2021, employees tallied 500,000 #MeMinutes—time spent doing things like meditating, listening to podcasts, or chatting with friends. Anthem’s interest in employee input doesn’t end with COVID-era programs. The company’s IdeaHub site allows staffers to share innovative ideas for the future. “The organization as a whole is transformational,” says one employee. “They are open to new ideas, and there is no discrimination based on who the idea comes from. This fosters a great work environment and allows everyone to be heard.”

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Elevance Health, formerly known as Anthem, experienced rapid growth during the public-health crisis created by COVID-19. In 2021, its profits increased by 33.5% compared with the prior year’s, and the company announced in early 2022 that it expects medical costs to remain at a high level in the near future owing to the pandemic. Meanwhile, the health insurer added about 30% more Medicare Advantage customers in 2021 than it did the previous year, enrolling 431,000 new members in the plans.

rankings.title: 100 Best Large Workplaces for Women
rankings.itemDescription:
Employees say:

“Having a CEO who is both a woman and an academic All-American athlete is highly inspirational, and her empathy and concern for our members and us, the Anthem associates, come across as very genuine. Gail also ensures her hiring practices for executive leadership are inclusive of women and people of color. On a separate note, Anthem worked hard to help us get through the pandemic, especially at the beginning stages, and supported both our physical and mental health. One thing that was especially helpful during that time, and that they have since continued, is our office fitness center vendor EXOS began leading video movement and stretch breaks: 15 minutes in the morning and 15 minutes in the afternoon, respectively.”

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: A new addition to Fortune’s Best Companies list, health care insurance provider Anthem is no stranger to medical care crises. As the pandemic reared its ugly head, the company moved aggressively to help its employees work through the global shutdown. It offered 80 hours of additional paid leave to those who were ill or had children, and also paid for the cost of COVID testing and treatment in full.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: America’s largest for-profit health insurance federation continues to roll on unabated, and, as with other industry titans, vertical integration has been its key to success in a tumultuous year. Controlling the length of a supply chain provides a bit of security in uncertain times, and Anthem’s pharmacy benefits arm IngenioRx has helped it do just that. The company’s 2020 revenue was just shy of $121 billion, a 17% increase over the previous year, assisted by a massive surge in Anthem’s Medicare Advantage business. The unit encompassing IngenioRx helped fuel a 9.3% year-over-year spike in first-quarter 2021 sales and is one of the company’s main focus areas going forward.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Anthem is the largest for-profit health insurer in the sprawling Blue Cross Blue Shield federation—a compendium that includes 36 independent and locally operated companies. In 2019, the company seized on a growth opportunity by officially launching its new pharmacy benefits arm, IngenioRx. Anthem president and CEO Gail Boudreaux, who was appointed to the top perch in late 2017, has emphasized the importance of that move, citing it as the main driver for the firm’s nearly 13% increase in year-over-year operating revenue. However, as with most major health insurers, a special tax waiver for 2019 boosted Anthem’s numbers. The company has about 41 million insured members across more than two dozen states.
